name: Secure Media Handling with Encryption
description: Enterprise-grade secure media handling with AES-256 encryption at rest, time-limited signed URLs, workspace-scoped encryption keys, and comprehensive audit logging for SOC2 and GDPR compliance.
goals: Protect customer media with AES-256 encryption at rest
Prevent direct access to R2 objects - all access through signed URLs
Provide comprehensive audit logging for SOC2 compliance
Support GDPR data portability and right to erasure
Enable secure key rotation without data loss
nonGoals: Client-side encryption (CSE) - handled separately for BYOS

rules: Each workspace has its own encryption key (derived from master key)
Encryption keys are never exposed to clients
Key rotation affects only the target workspace

workflows.name: Encrypted Upload Flow
steps: 1. Client requests upload session with gallery_id, sub_gallery_id, filename, mime_type
2. Backend generates upload_id and returns signed URL for temporary upload
3. Client uploads original file to temporary location
4. Client commits upload with SHA256 checksum
5. Backend verifies checksum and extracts metadata (EXIF)
6. Backend generates WebP preview (2048px) and thumbnail (512px)
7. Backend encrypts all three variants with workspace key
8. Backend uploads encrypted files to R2 with .enc extension
9. Backend stores encryption metadata (IV, auth_tag, key_version)
10. Backend deletes temporary unencrypted file
11. Backend returns asset_id and CDN URLs (which require signed tokens)

workflows.name: Decrypted View Flow
steps: 1. Client requests signed URL for asset variant
2. Backend verifies user permissions and workspace membership
3. Backend generates time-limited signed token (1 hour TTL)
4. Client requests media using signed token
5. Backend validates token signature and expiry
6. Backend fetches encrypted file from R2
7. Backend decrypts file using workspace key and stored IV
8. Backend streams decrypted content to client
9. Backend logs access for audit trail

workflows.name: Key Rotation Flow
steps: 1. Admin initiates key rotation
2. System generates new key version
3. System marks current key as 'rotating'
4. Background job iterates all assets encrypted with old key
5. For each asset: decrypt with old key, re-encrypt with new key
6. Update asset_encryption record with new key_version
7. When all assets migrated, mark old key as 'retired'
8. Notify admin of completion

accessControl: No public bucket access - all R2 objects private
Signed URLs required for all media access with 1-hour TTL
Workspace-scoped encryption keys with cryptographic isolation
Key material never exposed to clients or logs
Mandatory workspace_id filter on all database queries
JWT token validation on every API request
Session timeout: 15 minutes idle, 24 hours absolute
encryption: AES-256-GCM encryption for all media at rest
TLS 1.3 minimum for all data in transit
inputValidation: Parameterized queries for all database operations
Input sanitization and validation on all user inputs
File header (magic bytes) validation for uploads
MIME type verification against file content
Filename sanitization to prevent path traversal
webSecurity: CSRF tokens on all state-changing requests
rateLimiting: 100 requests/minute per IP for API endpoints
Progressive delays after failed login attempts
Account lockout after 5 failed attempts (15 minute cooldown)
Separate limits for media delivery endpoints
monitoring: Real-time anomaly detection for unusual access patterns
New IP/device detection with optional verification
